## Behaviour changes

- **In a remote window (SSH, a WSL window, a dev container, Codespaces) a terminal command is judged as read by an unknown shell, not by this machine's.** Such a command is never vouched read-only and never covered by an allow rule, so it follows your level; deny and ask rules read it under every grammar. Before, it was judged by the editor machine's shell (PowerShell on a Windows laptop for a command a remote bash reads). The command lint's dialect checks and the missing-program check no longer run for a remote window, so `cd app && npm test` is no longer refused on a Windows laptop before it reaches a remote bash.
- With `$SHELL` set to a shell the permission engine does not parse (fish, nushell, ksh), allow rules no longer cover terminal commands, in the IDE and in `cn` (`Bash(...)` rules): the call follows your level, and headless one that would ask is refused.
- Deny and ask rules read a PowerShell `-EncodedCommand` decoded, under every spelling PowerShell takes (`-e`, `-ec`, `-enc`, `/e`, any case, nested). One that cannot be decoded matches every deny and ask rule, and every floor rule. The audit record of a terminal command now names the shell it was read with and whether that is known (`reading.shell`, `reading.shellSource`).
